title: Advance on mastery, not completion
statement: Move a learner on only when rigorous checks of independent, unprompted performance show mastery, never for time spent, finishing or saying they know it.
detail: The delivery platform's non-negotiables require mastery gates at 90% accuracy or more and forbid advancing students on time, completion or self-report; its learning-science page says students do not progress without at least 90% accuracy on rigorous assessments, and its evaluation dimensions define mastery truthfulness as completed meaning mastered. The reading project adopted these as its bar. Recognising an answer with hints does not count as mastery either, so that completed means mastered.
against: The bar and its enforcement vary: one platform's mastery metric counts 80% correct (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0006-beyond-alpharead-source.qmd`, line 55), and one course plan stages its 90% gates, advisory at first and blocking later, with only about 17% reaching 90% today (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0007-ti-courseplans-repo.qmd`, line 123). The same page records a criticism of the approach: '- Sometimes criticized for being too rigid or prescriptive, potentially limiting teacher creativity' (`icloud-work/incept/incept-uae-api-website/bench.inceptapi.com/content/english/pages/direct-instruction.md`, line 62).

evidence.quote: 2. **Enforce mastery gates at ≥90% accuracy.** Do not advance students based on time, completion, or self-report.
Students do not progress without demonstrating ≥90% accuracy on rigorous assessments.
The **"mastery" metric (80% correct answers)** is accurately calculated on Dash.
**Staged 90% gates** — Band A advisory, blocking from Band B, final gate at course end (only ~17% reach 90% today).
Progression to the next lesson occurs only when students demonstrate mastery of current material.
Incept defines mastery as the point at which a student can apply a skill or concept independently, accurately, and automatically.
Every cycle ends with independent recall \- typing or saying the word without hints \- to confirm mastery.
This structured cycle ensures every new word moves from recognition to confident, fluent use.
Coached completion, engagement and fluent writing matter, but none can substitute for that evidence.
Do not infer mastery from task completion, a self-reported spoken repetition, an elapsed audio clip, or agreement with an example.
